rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies a very poor-quality early blastocyst with minimal cavitation and poorly defined/absent ICM and TE, consistent with the provided 0DD grade. Minor overstatement in calling it essentially noncavitating/nonviable from a single image and limited comment on zona/collapse nuance.
Strongly integrates age, ovarian reserve, prior cycle, semen parameters, diagnosis, and endometrial context with the dominant adverse effect of embryo morphology on prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with embryo quality appropriately driving prognosis. Slight tension between stating 5–10% and then suggesting many clinicians would say around 5% or less.

Generally aligned with Gardner grading interpretation and standard IVF counseling, including single embryo transfer and cautious use of PGT-A in a 31-year-old. Minor deviations include somewhat strong claims of nonviability from morphology alone and limited nuance around fresh transfer/endometrial thickness.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and future cycles, including luteal support, lab review, uterine evaluation if repeated failure, stimulation review, and lifestyle optimization. Useful though not highly protocol-specific.
